+_RISC-V Worlds_ provides isolation in a hardware platform by constraining
+access to system physical addresses. It provides _Worlds_, which are system
+partitions consisting of execution contexts (including agents, such as harts
+and devices, that can initiate a transaction on a physical address within a
+world) and resources (such as memories and peripheral devices, which respond to
+transactions at a physical address within a world). Worlds are created and
+configured by a trusted execution environment, usually at system boot time.
+
+Worlds are uniquely identified by a _World_ _Identifier_ (_WID_) that
+is associated with all outgoing transactions.
+The maximum number of unique WIDs on a platform is _NWorlds_. Increasing
+NWorlds increases the hardware cost, and in practice, 2-8 WIDs (requiring 1-3
+bits to represent) are sufficient for many use cases.
+
+Hardware agents (harts and devices) that can initiate transactions on physical
+addresses may support multiple contexts, with each context potentially being in
+a different world. As the WID to associate with outgoing transactions is
+typically determined by a control register, a given (software or hardware)
+context can only be present in one world at a time.
+
+Resources are identified by system physical addresses. A world may be granted
+some combination of access permissions on a physical
+address, meaning that emitted transactions will be examined by a WID-aware
+interface somewhere along the transaction path to enforce such permission
+checking. It is possible for a resource to be accessible via more than one WID,
+allowing for resource-sharing across worlds.
+
+_RISC-V Worlds_ is designed for the case where the allocation of
 agent contexts and resources to worlds is performed before or at
 reset/boot time, and not changed dynamically when the system is running
 unless there is a system reset.  Efficiently changing worlds allocation
 configurations dynamically while the system is running is not a goal of
 the current specification.

+When a hart attempts an explicit or implicit memory access that fails a World
+permissions check, the access may or may not raise an access-fault exception of
+the appropriate type (instruction-access fault, load-access fault, or
+store/AMO-access fault). The ability to raise an appropriate exception will be
+determined by where the permission-checking is being performed along the
+transaction's path (in the hart itself, at the transaction's target, or
+somewhere in between). When an access-fault exception cannot be raised, the
+instruction performing the memory access can be retired but any writes to the
+protected physical memory location are ignored and any memory reads return data
+independent of the value in the protected physical memory location to avoid
+violating memory isolation.
